answer: Escrowed interaction debt: each new identity must front a real deposit into a shared river of settlement funds before it can transact, and that deposit is forfeited to the counterparty whenever a signed exchange defaults. Because a clone cluster must post fresh deposits for every synthetic node, the marginal attacker cost rises linearly while expected yield falls toward a nadir as detection catches correlated defaults. Attackers wander across cheap throwaway accounts, but each pays a full forfeit before producing one unit of usable reputation, making the clone strictly negative-EV.
